objective: Prove that if at a lag every cell outside ring X holds nothing of X's born cells and X's own cells hold them independently, every contact binds X from then on exactly when it does in the static stage; that doubling every lag meets this at every lag, so with balanced stages every stage stays balanced at every lag; and compute, for doubling every P = 2, 3, 4, 6, 8 lags from the 3 x 3 tube at g = 2, whether rings stay isolated and stages balanced, to 48 x 48.
status: Proved 2026-11-09 (by hand; finite claims checked exactly; slower schedules computed): if no cell outside a ring holds its born cells and its own cells hold them independently, contacts bind it exactly as in the static stage; doubling every lag meets this at every lag, so every stage stays balanced at every lag. Computed: doubling every 2, 4, 6 or 8 lags breaks isolation and balance by 24 x 24; every 3 lags keeps both to 48 x 48.
title: Doubling every lag keeps every stage balanced; slower doubling does not
